title: Intersecting sets (A ∩ B ≠ φ)
reading: Circles overlap: sets ke beech common elements hain.

title: Disjoint sets (A ∩ B = φ)
reading: Circles overlap nahi karte: koi common element nahi.

title: Subset and equal sets
reading: A ⊆ B mein circle A circle B ke andar hota hai. A = B mein circles same hote hain.

title: Union A ∪ B
reading: Dono circles poore shade: A ya B mein jo bhi element ho.

title: Intersection A ∩ B
reading: Sirf overlap shade: dono sets ke common elements.

title: Complement A'
reading: Rectangle U mein circle A ke bahar ka hissa shade.

title: Difference A - B
reading: Circle A ka hissa jo circle B se bahar hai.

title: Difference B - A
reading: Circle B ka hissa jo circle A se bahar hai.

title: Symmetric difference A Δ B
reading: Sirf ek set mein aane wale elements: dono circles ka non-overlapping part.

title: Conjunction truth table (AND)
reading: p ∧ q sirf tab true hai jab dono true hon.

title: Disjunction truth table (OR)
reading: p ∨ q tab false hai jab dono false hon.

title: Conditional truth table (p → q)
reading: p → q sirf tab false hai jab p true aur q false ho.

title: Biconditional truth table (p ↔ q)
reading: p ↔ q tab true hai jab dono ki values same hon.

title: Tautology: p ∨ ~p
reading: Final column sab rows mein true: tautology.

title: Contradiction: p ∧ ~p
reading: Final column sab rows mein false: contradiction.

title: Example 1: (p ∨ ~q) → (p ∧ q)
reading: Step by step columns banao, last column answer hai.

title: Example 4: (p → q) → r
reading: Pehle p → q, phir uska r ke saath conditional.

title: Implication and equivalence: p → q and ~q → ~p
reading: Dono statements ki final columns same hain, isliye equivalent.

title: Distributive law: p ∧ (q ∨ r)
reading: LHS aur RHS ki final columns same: law verify.

title: Matrix notation and order
reading: Order m × n: m rows, n columns. a_ij = row i, column j.

title: Row, column and zero matrix
reading: Ek row = row matrix, ek column = column matrix, sab 0 = zero matrix.

title: Square, diagonal, scalar and identity matrix
reading: Diagonal: non-diagonal 0. Scalar: diagonal barabar. Identity: diagonal 1.

title: Upper and lower triangular matrix
reading: Upper triangular: diagonal ke neeche 0. Lower: diagonal ke upar 0.

title: Symmetric matrix: A = Aᵀ
reading: A = Aᵀ hai to matrix symmetric hai.

title: A² = I example
reading: A² = I: slide ka example, A × A karke identity milti hai.

title: 3 × 3 determinant by cofactor expansion
reading: 3 × 3 determinant: row 1 ke cofactor expansion, |A| = 0.

title: Minor matrix
reading: Har element ka minor: row aur column hatane ke baad bachi determinant.

title: Cofactor matrix
reading: Cofactor = sign × minor. Sign pattern + − + / − + − / + − +.

title: Adjoint = transpose of cofactor matrix
reading: Adjoint = cofactor matrix ka transpose.

title: 2 × 2 inverse by adjoint
reading: 2 × 2 inverse: |A| = 4, adj ko 4 se divide karo.

title: 3 × 3 inverse by adjoint
reading: 3 × 3 inverse: |A| = −3, cofactor, transpose, phir divide.

title: A' (complement) Venn
reading: Circle A ke bahar ka area (rectangle U ke andar) = A'.

title: Union A ∪ B (example)
reading: Dono circles ka poora area = A ∪ B.

title: Intersection A ∩ B (example)
reading: Sirf overlap = A ∩ B.

title: Three-set example: region table (U = 1..10)
reading: Teen sets A, B, C ke saare regions: kaun sa element kis region mein hai.

title: Four-set example: region table (U = divisors of 48)
reading: Divisors wala example: A, B, C ke regions.

title: Example with A, B, C (U = 11..20)
reading: A, B, C ke regions: 18 teeno/do sets mein kahan hai, dekho.

title: Example 2: (~p ∧ ~q) → (p ∨ q)
reading: Do variables wala statement: pehle NOT, phir AND/OR, last mein →.

title: Example 3(i): p ∨ q ∨ r and p ∧ q ∧ r
reading: Teen variables ka OR aur AND: OR sirf 000 par 0, AND sirf 111 par 1.

title: Example 5: (~p → q) → ~r
reading: Har intermediate column se final column nikalo.

title: Example 6: (~p ∧ q) → r
reading: Pehle ~p ∧ q, phir → r.

title: Example 7: ~[(p ∨ ~q) ∧ ~r]
reading: Andar se bahar: pehle p ∨ ~q, phir ∧ ~r, last mein NOT.

title: Example 8: ~(p ∨ q) → (~q ∨ r) (tautology)
reading: Sab 8 rows mein 1: tautology.

title: Example 9: (~p ∧ q) ∨ (~r ∧ q)
reading: Dono AND ka OR.

title: A·B (3 × 3 example)
reading: Row × column: A ki row aur B ki column ka dot product.

title: A·B (3 × 2 and 2 × 4)
reading: Inner dimensions match (2 = 2), order 3 × 4.

title: A·B (3 × 2 and 2 × 3)
reading: 3 × 2 aur 2 × 3 ka product 3 × 3 hota hai.

title: B·A (2 × 3 and 3 × 2)
reading: BA 2 × 2 hota hai, AB se alag (non-commutative).

title: adj(A) for A = [[1, 2, 3], [4, 3, 2], [1, 0, 3]]
reading: |A| = −20. adj(A) = cofactor matrix ka transpose.

title: adj(A) for A = [[−1, 2, 3], [−4, 0, 5], [0, 1, 2]]
reading: |A| = 9. adj(A) = Cᵀ.

title: Union and intersection (disjoint sets, U = 1..10)
reading: A = {1, 2, 4, 5} aur B = {6, 7, 9, 10} disjoint hain: union sab elements, intersection khaali.

title: Symmetric difference A Δ B (disjoint sets)
reading: Disjoint sets ka A Δ B = A ∪ B, kyunki overlap khaali hai.
